clue.text: Absurdly enough, set store by such favours

indicators.note: absurdly suggests the words set store are thrown into a ridiculous new order

explanation.surface: Someone sets great store, perhaps absurdly, by the small tokens of favour they receive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absurdly' tells you to rearrange SETSTORE; 'set store by' reads as a phrase meaning value, which hides the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Favours are ribbon badges worn as tokens, and rosettes are exactly such ribbon decorations.

clue.text: Re-classify a holiday place

explanation.surface: A resort town gets reclassified by the tourist board.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort again is to reclassify, written with a hyphen; a seaside town visited for holidays is also called this.

clue.text: He's maybe going round the bend — it's the examination!

indicators.note: going round says the shuffled letters surround the next piece like a loop
maybe signals that the letters of He's may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: the letters of He's taken as written, without the apostrophe
an arch or arc is a bend or curve

explanation.surface: Someone is driven round the bend by the stress of a looming examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's' looks like the subject of the sentence; 'maybe' marks its letters for rearranging, and 'going round' puts them around the bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A search is a careful examination, as in a search of a house or of records.

clue.text: Subject to ups and downs in the main'

definitions.text: Subject to ups and downs in the main

parts.words: Subject to ups and downs in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea, whose water rises and falls daily, while the surface reads as being up and down mostly

explanation.surface: Someone or something is, for the most part, subject to ups and downs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly', but here 'the main' is the old word for the open sea, whose level rises and falls.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's level rising and falling twice a day is caused by the moon's pull, described by this adjective.

clue.text: Oriental variety of sea-gull

indicators.note: a variety of the word sea means its letters in another arrangement

parts.note: a tern is a seabird related to the gull

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots an oriental variety of seagull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea-gull' reads as one bird, but the hyphen splits into the fodder 'sea' and the bird the gull stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from the East, especially Asia.

clue.text: Writer putting certain points about copy

indicators.note: about here means around, so the two points sit either side of the copy

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
to crib is to copy another's work

explanation.surface: A writer copies text while placing some points around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S and E (compass points) either side of CRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe was a professional copyist, one who wrote documents by hand.

clue.text: The crowd will get cold on the track

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a course is a racetrack, as in a racecourse

explanation.surface: A crowd at the racetrack will feel the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a large gathering or throng of people.

clue.text: Give it time, Edward said again

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Ted is a familiar short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward, told to give it time, repeats himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iterated has been repeated, stated a second time or more.

clue.text: 25 framing feed appeal

indicators.note: framing says one piece surrounds another like a picture frame

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, admission, means entry
to eat is to feed

explanation.surface: An appeal to be fed, given as a cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' is a cross-reference: the answer at 25-across is ADMISSION, and the wordplay needs its synonym, not the word itself; 'framing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or plea.

clue.text: Hit and smash, being careless

parts.note: to slap is to hit with an open hand
to dash something is to smash it, as in dashed to pieces

explanation.surface: Someone hits and smashes things with careless abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and carelessly.

clue.text: Nicest possible way to be a crawler

indicators.note: possible implies a possible rearrangement of the letters of Nicest

explanation.surface: A guide to the nicest way of being a toady or creep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawler' suggests a flatterer, as in 'the nicest way to crawl', but here it is a creeping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Many small six-legged creatures crawl, so a bug can be called a crawler.

clue.text: A break in hostilities to parley

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the words hostilities to parley

explanation.surface: A ceasefire in a war, arranged so that both sides can talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'hostilitieS TO Parley'; 'A break in hostilities' looks like the definition, a truce, but only 'A break' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is a pause or halt, a break in progress.

clue.text: Some serving men save, remember!

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers
to collect is to save up or gather

explanation.surface: An order to soldiers: save what you can, and remember it!
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) is a British Army corps, a crossword staple for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to recall to mind.

clue.text: Proclaim there's nothing to value

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing
to rate is to value or assess

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a thing has no value at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak formally and pompously, to declaim.

clue.text: Green-stuff

explanation.surface: A two-sided clue: grass, and stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassed area such as a bowling green is turf; lawn is also a fine linen fabric, and stuff means cloth.

clue.text: The sailor coloured and wouldn't have a drink

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
stained means coloured, as with dye

explanation.surface: A sailor, flushed with colour, refuses a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: AB (able-bodied seaman) is a standard crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to hold back from something, especially alcohol.

clue.text: Forecast the Left will retain ten

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A political forecast: the Left will hold on to ten seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Left' looks political but is the nautical left side of a ship; 'will retain' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen or sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Very very little drops from this

definitions.text: Very very little drops from this

parts.words: Very very little drops from this
parts.note: a spray bottle releases a fine mist of tiny droplets, read as something emptying very slowly

explanation.surface: A device from which hardly anything ever comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests almost nothing escapes, but the 'very very little drops' are the minute spray droplets of a perfume bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfume sprayer breaks liquid into minute droplets, almost particle-sized.

clue.text: Put off deals — she is without capital

indicators.note: put off suggests the letters of deals and she are disturbed and reordered

explanation.surface: She postpones business deals because she has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without capital' reads as having no funds; here it means lacking a head. 'Put off' rearranges DEALS and SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital is a head, so something without one has been beheaded.

clue.text: Set this out for religious people

indicators.note: out implies the letters of set this are set out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to set something out for a religious congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: People who believe in God are religious believers.

clue.text: The problem in combining tin with silver

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A metallurgist's difficulty in alloying tin with silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected difficulty or hitch.

clue.text: Dance with staggering results

explanation.surface: A dance that leaves the dancers unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish country dance has this name; to stagger or sway giddily is also to do this.

clue.text: Droll sorcerer making 2

definitions.note: the answer to 2 down, a search

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or droll
a mage is a magician or sorcerer

explanation.surface: A comic wizard performs his act, given as a cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' points to SEARCH at 2-down; RUM is British slang for strange or funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummage is a hunt through things, a disordered search.

clue.text: Hear the pound is to catch up

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to net is to catch, as with fish

explanation.surface: Hear how the pound is trying to catch up on the markets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NET to TEN, giving L + IS + TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to pay attention to sound, to hear.

clue.text: Access taken here — of course

explanation.surface: An entrance to a place where one dines, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrée means the right of entry; it is also a dish served as one part of a meal.

clue.text: Means taking some immediate action

indicators.note: some tells you that only part of the word immediate is needed

explanation.surface: A plan that involves taking immediate action.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is imMEDIAte.
explanation.definitionFit: Media are channels or methods, means of doing something, as in plural of medium.

clue.text: A large number aim for 23

definitions.note: the answer to 23 down, an entrée

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a mission is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Many people aiming for something, given as a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' refers to ENTREE at 23-down, meaning access.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is the right of entry to a place.

clue.text: View a lot

explanation.surface: A two-word clue: a view, and plenty of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is informal, as in 'a sight better' meaning a great deal better.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is a scene or vista; informally it also means a great deal, as in 'a sight too much'.

clue.text: The author might well be tenser!

indicators.note: might well be says the letters of tenser could be rearranged into a name

explanation.surface: A writer could very well be rather tense.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne is the 18th-century writer of Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: "— holding both his sides" (Milton)

parts.note: a line from Milton's poem L'Allegro, describing a figure doubled up with mirth

explanation.surface: A gap-fill from Milton: what is shown holding both his sides?
explanation.walkthrough: The line in L'Allegro runs 'And ___ holding both his sides', personifying mirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone convulsed with mirth clutches their sides, the posture the poem gives to merriment personified.

clue.text: Stay concerned with the players

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a side is a team of players

explanation.surface: Someone stays involved with the team.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live or stay in a place.

clue.text: Time for a few words?

explanation.surface: A judge gives a prisoner time in a few words.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term is time served; a grammatical unit of a few words also has this name.
